test.name: Spec 0011 step 7: Deny and Cancel on the login Keychain dialog through stacklyd

expected: With stacklyd on the default root and an item in the login Keychain made by an earlier build, secret.reveal from an interactive client shows the Keychain dialog; pressing Deny and dismissing with Cancel or Escape each end the call without a value, each maps to a stable secret.* error code (the spike on the file keychain recorded errSecUserCanceled for both), and the codes and the dialog labels are noted
actual: 2026-10-24: created a disposable generated reference on the default login Keychain, revision 1, exit 0. Restarted stacklyd from a copy with a different ad hoc signing identifier and launched an interactive reveal. The call waited for native authorization. Computer use explicitly refused access to com.apple.SecurityAgent, so no Deny or Cancel action, dialog wording, or resulting error is claimed. Cancelled the client, stopped the daemon, and deleted the disposable reference. See docs/reviews/2026-10-24-f11-native-followup.md.
reason: The computer use tool refuses access to com.apple.SecurityAgent for safety reasons. A GUI login session exists, but the required authorization dialog cannot be inspected or controlled with the available permitted interface.
owner: Native Keychain dialog verification with an authorized interactive operator
steps: In a Terminal at the repo root, build both binaries: `cargo build -q -p stacklyd -p stackly-cli`.

Terminal A: start the daemon on the DEFAULT root (no STACKLY_ROOT, so it uses the login Keychain, and it creates ~/Library/Application Support/Stackly if absent): `cargo run -q -p stacklyd`. Leave it running.

Terminal B (a real Terminal, nothing piped, so the client is interactive): `cargo run -q -p stackly-cli -- secret set local:user/manual-keychain-check --generate`. Expect exit 0; note whether any Keychain dialog appeared (none is expected for the build that made the item).

Terminal A: press Ctrl-C to stop the daemon. Then `touch apps/daemon/src/main.rs && cargo build -q -p stacklyd` (a new ad hoc build, so a new code identity), and start it again with `cargo run -q -p stacklyd`.

Terminal B: `cargo run -q -p stackly-cli -- secret reveal local:user/manual-keychain-check`. A Keychain dialog should appear. Click Deny. Note: the CLI exit code, the error code printed (run again with `--json` if the text is unclear), and the dialog's buttons.
Run the same reveal again. This time dismiss the dialog with the Cancel button if it has one, or the Escape key if not. Note the same three things.
Note whether the two outcomes gave the same `secret.*` error code and whether the second run showed the dialog again.

Cleanup: `cargo run -q -p stackly-cli -- secret delete local:user/manual-keychain-check`, then `security delete-generic-password -s stackly-secret -a user/manual-keychain-check` (ignore 'could not be found'), then Ctrl-C the daemon in Terminal A.
Write down the macOS version and the exact dialog wording and button labels you saw.
